title: Five samples. One traceable laboratory journey.

steps.title: One platform, several working languages
steps.caption: Role-specific access, with English, Spanish, French and Portuguese interface options.
steps.say: This is SoilFER LIMS. Staff use role-specific workspaces with multilingual interface options. In three minutes, we will follow five demonstration samples from field collection to reviewed laboratory information.

steps.title: Start with the work that matters
steps.caption: Each role opens on its own work and exceptions.
steps.say: Each person opens on the work that needs their attention: reception, analysis or review.

steps.title: The field record travels with the sample
steps.caption: Kobo supplies sample identity, collection details and field context. Expected is not received.
steps.say: These five samples belong to SOILFER-US. Kobo brings their field identity, collection details and location into the laboratory record. They remain expected samples until staff record their physical arrival.

steps.title: Check the material, then accept it
steps.caption: Match the label, inspect condition and quantity, and confirm the requested analyses.
steps.say: Reception matches each container to its field record, checks condition and quantity, and confirms the requested analyses. Here are all five intake receipts. Each sample now has a laboratory identity and a recorded handover.

steps.title: People, instruments and supplies, connected
steps.caption: Assign the work; check equipment readiness and laboratory stock.
steps.say: The manager assigns the work to staff using the selected methods. Equipment records show instrument readiness and maintenance. Inventory provides visibility of laboratory supplies, helping the team prepare for the work ahead.

steps.title: Prepare the material before analysis
steps.caption: Recorded drying and preparation checks make the next work available.
steps.say: Drying and preparation follow the laboratory procedure and leave a recorded checklist. They take real time. This presentation moves to a prepared demonstration checkpoint; it does not perform those physical operations instantly.

steps.title: One analysis bench for the whole batch
steps.caption: Five pH readings in one worksheet. Sand, silt and clay stay together as texture.
steps.say: At the analysis bench, the technician works by method across the batch. Five pH readings share one worksheet. Texture keeps sand, silt and clay together. Drafts, recorded results and submissions remain distinct.

steps.title: Keep the spectrum, not just a number
steps.caption: MIR and NIR use instrument files, with their sample identity and quality checks.
steps.say: MIR and NIR analysis use spectra exported from instruments. The file, sample identity and quality information remain linked. The spectral library lets staff inspect this evidence rather than retype a single number.

steps.title: Review the evidence before release
steps.caption: Submitted work is reviewed with its quality checks. Problems can be returned with a reason.
steps.say: The manager reviews submitted results and quality checks, then accepts or returns the work with a reason. A newly received sample cannot qualify for approval simply because it is in the system.

steps.title: See the whole journey, then the report
steps.caption: The workflow map explains dependencies. Reports preserve the reviewed evidence and its history.
steps.say: The workflow map shows each stage and its dependencies. The sample record connects that journey to reviewed results and versioned reports. A value can be traced back to its method, operator and supporting evidence.

steps.title: Connect laboratory work to national information
steps.caption: SIS means Soil Information System. This is an exchange preview, not a claimed live delivery.
steps.say: The exchange interface connects laboratory information with national Soil Information Systems. Here we preview sample identity, location and results together. The receiving national team will validate its connection during the pilot.

steps.title: Next: controlled testing in a real laboratory
steps.caption: Agree the pilot laboratory, operators and acceptance checks.
steps.say: Our next step is controlled real-laboratory testing. We will agree the operators, sign off the workflow checks and collect feedback on traceability, reliable daily work and reviewed results.
